questions.prompt: Which item is described as useful but not required?
questions.explanation: A hotspot can help when Wi-Fi is unreliable, but it is optional.

questions.prompt: An electronic task is available ahead of time. What should you do?

options.text: Analyze it and prepare relevant research
Ignore it until the round starts

questions.explanation: Advance access is an opportunity to prepare without preempting the group's decisions.

questions.prompt: The tournament specifies an assigned seating order. What takes priority?

options.text: Your preferred seat near the judge

questions.explanation: Follow the directions for the specific tournament and round.

questions.prompt: What is the main purpose of pre-round small talk?

options.text: Build rapport and a cooperative tone
Rank classmates as allies or opponents
Take control before the timer starts.

questions.explanation: Icebreakers prepare people to work together; they are not an extra competition.

questions.prompt: Someone dominates the pre-round conversation. What is the best response?

options.text: Assume they will always be difficult
Use that early impression to plan a role that fits the group's procedural and substantive needs

questions.explanation: Pre-round behavior can help you anticipate group dynamics. If procedural roles are crowded, focus more on substantive contributions; if the group is more passive, be ready to set agendas, keep time, and encourage participation. Adjust as the round develops.
